decisions.executionNote: Begin raised elbow-up approaches to red nut on left and purple nut on right; slow orientation changes from home.
Complete downward-facing orientation and approach above red and purple nuts, keeping each arm on its own side.
Wrist views show lateral offsets; make small visual corrections and descend to nut-grasp height, without closing yet.
Refine nut centering from wrist images, then close both grippers. Retention remains to be checked on lift.
Lift both nuts and begin moving toward their matching screws while maintaining closed grippers; verify retention in the new views.
Carry red nut above red screw and lower purple nut toward its matching screw. Both nuts remain visibly held; check coaxial alignment before twisting.
Small centering corrections followed by a slow clockwise threading stroke on both matched pairs; depth and engagement remain visually uncertain.
Continue the clockwise stroke with a small axial feed, then open and reset wrist rotation without lifting the nuts.
Regrasp the seated nuts and apply a second slow clockwise tightening stroke with a small downward feed.
Open before resetting both wrists, leaving the nuts on their matching screws for another tightening stroke.
Regrasp and tighten both nuts another quarter turn with gentle axial feed, observing the screw ends rising inside the holes.
Release and reset wrists while keeping the nuts seated. Purple appears deeper than red; neither pair is assumed complete.
Apply another controlled clockwise stroke to each nut after regrasping, maintaining upright axes and closed grippers.
Open and reset wrist yaw without backing the nuts off, preparing a further tightening stroke.
Continue red tightening; give the deeper purple pair a shorter finishing stroke, release it, and start withdrawing vertically.
Reset the left wrist for another red tightening stroke. Withdraw the open right gripper and move above the gray nut, leaving purple undisturbed.
Continue tightening red while moving the open right gripper to the gray nut's calibrated vicinity and descending cautiously.
Reset the open left wrist while centering and lowering the right gripper around the gray nut. Inspect before closing.
Tighten red further while grasping and lifting the centered gray nut; verify gray retention before transferring toward the middle.
Reset the open left wrist and carry the visibly retained gray nut inward at clearance height, staying in the right workspace.
Give red another tightening stroke while carrying gray to the center staging area, keeping the right arm on its side.
Reset and raise the left grasp slightly to recenter on the red nut body. Lower the held gray nut at the central staging point without crossing arms.
Regrasp red higher on its body for a clockwise stroke without axial forcing. Release gray at center and withdraw the right hand.
Reset the open left wrist for a finishing red stroke and move the right arm clear of the staged gray nut.
Finish another red tightening stroke and begin returning the open right arm along a raised, configuration-continuous path.
Release red before resetting its wrist. Complete the right arm's return toward home while leaving the staged gray nut undisturbed.
Another finishing clockwise stroke on red, with minimal axial feed; keep the right arm open at home.
Release the red pair and withdraw vertically while resetting the left wrist for the staged gray nut.
Move the open left hand above the central gray nut for table-mediated transfer; right arm stays at home.
Descend slowly over the staged gray nut with the left gripper open, keeping its EE on the left side of center.
Correct the visible gray-nut offset at the central handover area, close the left gripper, and make a short retention-check lift.
Gray is visibly retained. Raise it above the assembled parts, then carry it left toward its matching screw with the right arm parked.
Move gray over its matching screw in the left workspace, then lower to the initial insertion height for visual alignment.
Wrist view shows the gray screw offset to the right of the nut. Correct laterally in small increments, then lower slightly before threading.
Gray axes now appear nearly aligned. Make a millimeter-scale correction and begin clockwise threading with gentle axial feed.
Release, reset, and regrasp gray for another short clockwise tightening stroke; keep the other pairs untouched.
Continue the gray nut's release-reset-regrasp tightening cycle with a small axial feed, monitoring its seated depth.
Open the gray grasp and reset farther within wrist limits, preparing a longer tightening stroke without disturbing its axial seating.
Regrasp gray and apply a longer clockwise tightening stroke with two millimeters of axial feed, maintaining alignment.
Release and reset the left wrist for continued gray tightening; keep the matching parts seated and the right hand parked.
Regrasp and continue clockwise threading of gray with a small axial feed. Monitor the screw end rising inside the nut.
Open before the return rotation, preserving the gray nut's threaded position for the next tightening stroke.
Continue gray tightening with a closed grasp and reduced axial feed, watching for the screw end approaching the nut face.
Open and reset gray, raising the grasp slightly to stay on the nut body rather than pressing downward as threading progresses.
Regrasp gray higher on the nut body and tighten clockwise without further downward forcing, checking whether the nut advances.
Release and reset the gray wrist while leaving the nut seated, preparing another finishing stroke.
Continue clockwise tightening of the gray nut with a small axial feed and a closed grasp; other pairs remain undisturbed.
Release and reset the gray wrist without lifting the nut, preserving its threaded depth for the next stroke.
Regrasp gray and apply another clockwise finishing stroke with minimal axial feed; inspect remaining exposed threads afterward.
Release the gray pair and withdraw vertically while resetting the wrist; inspect all three seated pairs and begin returning home.
All three pairs remain upright after release. Return the open left arm along a gradual elbow-up path, with the right arm at home.
Complete the gradual return to both original EE poses with both grippers open; the assembled pairs remain on the table.
